_readme: Caption looks: how the words on screen look and move. A look is a SETTING — switching it never re-edits the footage. Sizes are for a 1080-wide frame. `font` is a font id from looks/fonts.json (never a CSS stack). `zone` is where the line sits — a zone id from looks/placement.json (it moves off a face by itself when production marks one). `word_spacing` / `letter_spacing` are CSS lengths (`normal` = the font's own space, one space between words — no extra margin is ever added; an outlined look adds 0.1em so the outline does not eat the gap). `match-swipe` is not a row: it means build a one-off look from the teardown's caption read (font weight, case, colour, highlight, position). Only the owner signs a row approved.

looks.name: Bold highlight
looks.what: Big white capitals with a black outline, 2–4 words at a time, the word being spoken turns yellow and pops.
looks.when_to_use: The default for talking-head ads: loud, readable with the sound off, the spoken word lit.

looks.name: Clean lower
looks.what: Sentence-case white words on a soft dark plate, low in the frame. Reads like a subtitle, not a shout.
looks.when_to_use: Calm, premium or clinical pieces; long sentences; an expert talking.

looks.name: One word
looks.what: One huge word at a time, dead centre. For hooks and fast cuts.
looks.when_to_use: Hooks and fast montage where each word is a hit.

looks.name: Word box
looks.what: Bold white capitals, 2–3 words at a time; the word being sung or said sits on a coloured box that moves word to word.
looks.when_to_use: Song ads and lyric-led pieces: the box rides the sung word (the owner, 2026-10-10, the first song ad — the swipe's box sat behind each sung word).
